a.summary: Switching the decoder from the shared `RpcEncoding` to a private `DataEncoding` copy drops the compile-time guarantee that sava can decode every encoding it can request; a future request encoding now silently decodes to an empty byte array instead of failing the build.
a.failure_scenario: Add a fourth constant to `RpcEncoding` (e.g. `base64_lz4("base64+lz4")`, or any future Solana encoding) and its `PARSER` arm, then call `ProgramAccountsRequest.build().encoding(RpcEncoding.base64_lz4)...`. The client emits `"encoding":"base64+lz4"` (ProgramAccountsRequestRecord.java:44), the node replies `["<payload>","base64+lz4"]`, `DATA_ENCODING_PARSER` falls through to `return null` (JsonUtil.java:39), and `case null -> new byte[0]` (JsonUtil.java:78) hands every `AccountInfo.data()` an empty array — no exception, and unlike the non-array fallback at line 85 not even a WARNING log. Before this commit the identical change did not compile: `switch (encoding)` at old line 58 was an exhaustive enum switch expression over `RpcEncoding` with no `default`, so adding a constant produced a compile error in JsonUtil that forced the decoder to be updated in lockstep.

b.summary: `DATA_ENCODING_PARSER` duplicates `RpcEncoding.PARSER`'s wire-name matching, leaving two independent copies of the same table and no production caller for the public `RpcEncoding.parseEncoding`.
b.failure_scenario: sava-rpc later adds a request encoding to `RpcEncoding` (the enum's own javadoc discusses which wire encodings belong there, so this is an expected kind of change) and wires it into `RpcEncoding.PARSER`. `DATA_ENCODING_PARSER` is a separate private copy and is not updated, so a node response whose data array carries that encoding falls to `return null` at JsonUtil.java:39, then to `case null -> new byte[0]` at line 78. `parseEncodedData` returns an empty account payload instead of the decoded data and instead of an error - the caller sees a zero-length account rather than a decode failure. RpcEncodingTests only exercises the request enum, so nothing in the suite would notice.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.
